systems.theater: None (not yet deployed). Trials at MOD Hebrides Range, Scotland and Dstl Porton Down, England; initial fit to two Royal Navy Type 45 destroyers with a stated objective of four
systems.targets: UAS (Class 1-2 target drones incl. Banshee); intended against fast inshore attack craft and ISR sensors
systems.effects: DragonFire destroyed 30 drone targets across more than 300 shots at UK ranges from March to June 2025, then downed high-speed drones flying at 650 km/h at the MOD Hebrides Range in October-November 2025. No combat use has been reported.
systems.description: DragonFire is a 50-kilowatt-class laser directed energy weapon (LDEW) developed for the UK Ministry of Defence by MBDA UK with Leonardo UK and QinetiQ under a Defence Science and Technology Laboratory (Dstl) capability demonstrator program. It is intended to give Royal Navy Type 45 destroyers a low-cost-per-shot close-in defense against uncrewed aerial systems and other small air and surface threats, with first ship installation planned for 2027.
systems.notes: Meets criterion 5 on the testing limb: repeated Dstl-led live-fire campaigns at MOD Hebrides Range (Q4 2023/Jan 2024; Oct-Nov 2025) and the Mar-Jun 2025 campaign in an operationally relevant containerised configuration, with a production (MDC) contract but no fielded system before 2027. Coded B1 on evidence: automated detection, tracking, aimpoint hold and beam dwell are documented; engagement initiation appears operator-authorized (MBDA single-operator design; UK human-involvement policy). Key uncertainty: whether MDC integration with the Type 45 combat management system (which supports automatic engagement modes for Sea Viper) will give DragonFire an operator-supervised automatic select-and-engage mode; if so, recode A2. Secondary uncertainty: sources disagree on the venue of the Mar-Jun 2025 300-shot campaign (Naval Technology: Porton Down; Janes: Hebrides). Function-level coding is evidence-based, not inherited from Iron Beam (ISR-LAND-005).
